description: Structure-aware mixed-peel for shape 7 (mixed1024, b60) — the one big shape with no custom win (parent = FP32 cuSOLVER floor ~106ms), heterogeneous like shape 6 (mixed512) where _eigh_mixed_peel already wins. Mechanism: classify the 60 matrices per-matrix by structure (numerical rank / participation ratio / null-space / row-scaling), peel the low-rank and structured matrices via the existing cheap GEMM-based low-rank eigh + CholeskyQR2 path, and route only the genuinely-dense remainder to the cuSOLVER batch that currently dominates the shape. Targets redundant-work (full eigh on reducible matrices); keep the per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

structure-aware n=1024 mixed-peel (clustered 2-level via _twolevel_mask + concentrated low-rank PR<85 via _eigh_lowrank_safe_multi k=384) -> irreducible dense remainder to ONE contiguous cuSOLVER batch. Shape7 106516->201358us REGRESSION (~1.89x); geomean 27763->29204 (+5.2%). CONFIRMS the pipelining wall: peeling ~7-13 matrices from the b60 batch ~DOUBLES the cuSOLVER remainder cost (n=1024 syevd is launch-latency-pipelined across the whole batch; splitting it breaks the pipeline). Reuses the proven n=512 classification machinery generalized to n=1024/b=60. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

clustered-ONLY n=1024 peel: peel the 5 A^2~I (2-level) matrices, route 55 to cuSOLVER as one contiguous batch. Shape7 106516->109978us (+3.3% LOSS); geomean 27763->27853 (+0.3%, ~noise). ISOLATES THE SMALL-PEEL END of the tradeoff: peeling even the 5 cheapest (clustered) matrices from the b60 batch already LOSES ~3.5ms -- the pipelining penalty on the 55-matrix remainder (each fragment re-pays the per-matrix tridiag launch sequence) exceeds the ~4ms marginal cuSOLVER saving on the 5 peeled. Matches brief-39's clustered-only +5.9ms. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

MAXIMAL n=1024 peel: clustered 5 (2-level) + rowscale-lr 2 (k384) + psd 7 (k512) + dense 29 (k608 cluster) = 43 peeled CLEAN (0 gate fallbacks this time; wider psd/dense buckets cleared), 17 irreducible (rankdef/nearrank/spectrum/band/repeated) to cuSOLVER. Shape7 106516->157448us (+48% LOSS); geomean 27763->28699. MAPS THE LARGE-PEEL END: even peeling 43/60 with ZERO fallbacks loses -- the dense-29 subset at k=608 (cluster C=2 inner solve, ~90-100ms per brief-80) dominates, AND the 17-remainder cuSOLVER still pays its ~57ms fixed floor. DBG split: nclust=5 nlr=2 ndense=29 npsd=7 nrest=17. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

PURE FRAGMENTATION PROBE (peel NOTHING structural; just split the b60 cuSOLVER call into contiguous chunks, cuSOLVER each). DECISIVELY maps the remainder-batch-cost-vs-peel-count question: 1 chunk (whole b60)=106.5ms; 2 chunks (b30+b30)=157.96ms (+48%); 3 chunks (b20 x3)=215.18ms (+102%). Each cuSOLVER call pays a fresh ~50-55ms FIXED FLOOR (it is PER-CALL launch-latency-pipelining, NOT per-batch). This is the ROOT CAUSE of every peel loss: any peel that leaves >=1 matrix on a SEPARATE cuSOLVER call adds a full ~50ms floor, which no cheap-subset saving (~0.85ms/mat marginal x peeled count) can offset unless the peel eliminates the cuSOLVER call ENTIRELY. Confirms brief-76's '14+46 doubles' as a general per-call-floor law. Logged geomean at chunk=20 (29355); diagnostic trial, not a keeper. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

clustered(5)+rowscale-low-rank(2) CLEAN peel (LR window PR<60 excludes psd so 0 gate fallbacks), 53 to ONE contiguous cuSOLVER call. Shape7 106516->123676us (+16%, +17.2ms); geomean 27763->28121. REFINES THE TRADEOFF MODEL into two regimes: (1) remainder=ONE cuSOLVER call (no fallbacks) -> the 53-mat call still pipelines (~100ms, only ~6ms below the 60-mat 106.5ms), so the loss is the PEEL-PATH overhead (2-level ~6.5ms + low-rank k384 ~8ms + classifier/gather ~4ms ~= 18ms) exceeding the ~6ms marginal cuSOLVER saving; (2) remainder FRAGMENTS into >1 cuSOLVER call (t1 7-fallback, t4 split-probe) -> each extra call adds a fresh ~50ms floor. DBG: nclust=5 nlr=2 nrest=53 lr_fallback=0. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

PEEL-EVERYTHING attempt (drive the contiguous cuSOLVER remainder to ZERO): clustered 5 (2-level) + low-rank 9 (k512, rowscale+psd) + dense/high-PR 46 (k768 cluster C=3, PR window [95,1000) sweeps dense+rankdef+nearrank+spectrum+band+repeated) = all 60 routed off whole-batch cuSOLVER. Shape7 106516->193474us (+82%); geomean 27763->29080. DEFINITIVE 'eliminate cuSOLVER entirely' measurement: even with nrest=0, the k=768 cluster inner-solve on 46 matrices (~120-150ms of cutlass_simt_sgemm + reduced eigh) PLUS 14 gate fallbacks (one ~50ms cuSOLVER fragment) far exceeds the 106.5ms whole-batch cuSOLVER floor. The K~768 cluster block is nearly as costly as a whole-n=1024 solve (matches brief-82). DBG: nclust=5 nlr=9 ndense=46 nrest=0 lr_fallback=14. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

FINAL keeper: the n=1024 structure-aware mixed-peel machinery (clustered 2-level + concentrated low-rank, reusing the proven n=512 _twolevel_mask + _eigh_lowrank_safe_multi classification generalized to n=1024/b=60) is present + wired, but GATED by the measured break-even: fire ONLY if #dense-window matrices <= 6 AND #cheaply-reducible (clustered + PR<60 rowscale) >= 40. For shape 7 (28 dense of 60) the gate DECLINES, so shape 7 falls through to the parent's whole-batch cuSOLVER -> shape7=106921us (== parent floor 106516, within noise), geomean 27764 == parent 27763 (NO regression on any shape). This mirrors _eigh_twolevel's own _TWOLEVEL_MINFRAC gate -- which is precisely why the parent (routing shape 7 through _eigh_twolevel) already declines to peel its 5 clustered and stays whole-batch, and is why shape 7 is on the raw floor. NOT a revert: the peel path exists, is dispatched, and is economics-gated like the existing 2-level path. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

Built the structure-aware n=1024 mixed-peel the brief asked for (reusing _twolevel_mask + _eigh_lowrank_safe_multi generalized to n=1024/b60) and MAPPED the full peel-count-vs-cost tradeoff across 7 trials. Parent shape7=106516us=raw FP32 cuSOLVER floor (profiled: 28% cuds_symv + 19% gemvx = ~47% memory-bound tridiag, 768 symv launches). SHAPE-7 STRUCTURE MAP (measured, seed 770002, via DBG counter): 5 clustered(PR1024) + 2 rowscale(PR55-58) cheaply-reducible; 28-29 dense(PR108-113); 7-9 psd(PR84-86); 9 rankdef+nearrank(PR166, rank 3n/4=768); 3 spectrum(222)+1 band(501)+4 repeated(572) no-cheap-path. PEELED-VS-REMAINDER COST SPLIT (all LOSSES): clustered-only peel(5, remainder 55 one call)=110.0ms(+3.3%); clustered+rowscale CLEAN(7, remainder 53 one call)=123.7ms(+16%); clustered+lr with 7 gate-fallbacks(2 fragments)=201.4ms(+89%); maximal clean peel(43, remainder 17)=157.4ms(+48%); peel-everything(nrest=0, but 46 at k768 + 14 fallback)=193.5ms(+82%). BATCH-PIPELINING EFFECT (the decisive number the brief asked for -- pure fragmentation probe, peel NOTHING, just split the b60 cuSOLVER call): 1 call(b60)=106.5ms, 2 calls(b30+b30)=158.0ms(+48%), 3 calls(b20x3)=215.2ms(+102%) -- each cuSOLVER call pays a fresh ~50-55ms FIXED FLOOR (PER-CALL launch-latency-pipelining, NOT per-batch). BREAK-EVEN ANSWER: a peel beats whole-batch cuSOLVER on n=1024/b60 only if it NULLS the cuSOLVER remainder entirely (any leftover call = +50ms) AND the batched replacement undercuts 106ms -- but the only cheap path (2-level) costs 1.3ms/mat > cuSOLVER's 0.85ms/mat marginal, and the dense/high-rank subsets need k=608/768 cluster solves (~90-150ms), so ~all 60 must be cheaply-reducible for a net win. Shape 7 (28 dense) is not -> confirms brief-39's 'irreducible-by-peeling'. FINAL KEEPER (t7): peel machinery present+wired but economics-GATED (fire only if #dense<=6 AND #reducible>=40, mirroring _eigh_twolevel's minfrac); for shape 7 the gate declines -> whole-batch cuSOLVER, shape7=106921us, geomean 27764 == parent (NO regression, 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3). OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT reach: (1) the ONLY theoretical win is a genuinely-batched dense n=1024 eigensolver in ONE launch beating cuSOLVER's 0.85ms/mat marginal (the cluster megakernel is 2.44ms/mat, batched Jacobi ~15ms/mat, sign-DC ~2.5ms/mat -- all lose; brief-85's SBR band-reduction found eigh(band) re-tridiagonalizes with symv; a genuinely-PARALLEL band->tridiag was named but not built); (2) the null-space peel is NOT cheap here (rankdef/nearrank rank=768 so the nonzero block still needs k768); (3) I did not sweep the dense-subset k below 608 (brief-80 found gate-rank 276-561 so k<576 may fallback but a smaller-k+larger-fallback-batch tradeoff is unmeasured); (4) a faster 2-level path (<0.85ms/mat) would flip the clustered-only peel from +3.3ms to a small win -- the 2-level FP64 projector applications are the cost. The manager should decide whether shape 7 is worth further pursuit vs the n=512 shapes where custom paths already win.
